proposals.before: On leaving the purple he was made Secretariat Gentleman of Liang and promoted to groom of the heir apparent.
proposals.after: On doffing coarse cloth he was made Secretariat Gentleman of Liang and promoted to groom of the heir apparent.
proposals.reason: 解褐 means doffing homespun to enter office, not leaving the purple.

proposals.before: When Emperor Wen governed Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the firm-resolution establishment and soon promoted him to left chief secretary of the secretariat.
proposals.after: When Emperor Wen governed Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the firm-resolution establishment and soon promoted him to left chief secretary of the Minister of Education.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister of Education, not the secretariat or Minister of Works.

proposals.before: When Emperor Wen was interior administrator of Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the Firm Resolution establishment and promoted him to left chief secretary of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: When Emperor Wen was interior administrator of Kuaiji, he again made Ji chief secretary of the Firm Resolution establishment and promoted him to left chief secretary of the Minister of Education.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister of Education, not the Secretariat or Minister of Works.

proposals.before: At that time Emperor Wu sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with gifts. Chang had Zai draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and the text needed no correction. Huang reported this to Emperor Wu, and Zai was soon summoned as compiler-historian.
proposals.after: At that time Emperor Wen sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with gifts. Chang had Zai draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and the text needed no correction. Huang reported this to Emperor Wen, and Zai was soon summoned as compiler-historian.
proposals.reason: 世祖 is Chen Shizu Emperor Wen, not Emperor Wu; 高祖 is Founder/Wu.

proposals.before: At that time Emperor Wu sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with various goods; Chang entrusted Zai to draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and fluent and the text needed no correction; when Huang returned he reported this to Emperor Wu, and soon Zai was summoned as compiler-historian.
proposals.after: At that time Emperor Wen sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with various goods; Chang entrusted Zai to draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and fluent and the text needed no correction; when Huang returned he reported this to Emperor Wen, and soon Zai was summoned as compiler-historian.
proposals.reason: 世祖 is Chen Shizu Emperor Wen, not Emperor Wu.

proposals.before: The imperial edict has already soared into the vast sky, [5] yet the apprehensive still peek into marshes seeking it.
proposals.after: The jiaoming bird has already soared into the boundless sky, [5] yet the hunter still searches the marshes for it.
proposals.reason: The corrected 鷦敕 denotes the jiaoming bird, while 虞者 is a hunter; this is not an imperial edict.

proposals.before: At the time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong; his family for generations were farmers—to Hua alone he loved learning, associated with gentlemen and scholars, and broadly read the classics and histories, skilled at composition.
proposals.after: At the time there was Zhang Hua of Wuxing, styled Zhongzong; his family for generations were farmers—Hua alone loved learning, associated with gentlemen and scholars, and broadly read the classics and histories, skilled at composition.
proposals.reason: Literal English has a broken subject (“to Hua alone he loved learning”); the Chinese 至華獨好學 means Hua alone loved learning.

decisions.reason: 解褐 is the formula for doffing coarse cloth to take office; “leaving the purple” invents 紫 and mistranslates 褐.
司徒左長史 is left chief secretary under the Minister of Education (司徒), not under the secretariat; 司空 would be Minister of Works.
Same office string 司徒左長史; replacing Secretariat with Minister of Education restores the Three Dukes title.
時世祖使…言之世祖 names Shizu; in Chen that is Emperor Wen, while Emperor Wu is 高祖.
